attempts.raw_response: If the dough is too sticky, dust your work surface and rolling pin with a little more cornstarch. If it is too dry and cracks at the edges, knead in a few drops of water until it comes together smoothly. Once you have achieved the right thickness, you are ready to cut it to size. Place your phone gently on top of the sheet and use a knife or pizza cutter to trim around it, leaving a narrow border of about half an inch on all sides. This extra margin will shrink slightly during baking, ensuring your final piece fits your device perfectly. Carefully transfer the cut sheet onto a piece of parchment paper.

pair.human_continuation: Make sure that your screen is facing upwards, and you have equal amounts (or close to it) of dough sticking out over each side. Slide a paint spatula under the dough, then lift it up and fold the dough over the sides of the phone. Smooth out any creases or wrinkles; try to be as neat as possible. Flip your phone over and dust it with cornstarch. Use a stamp to indent designs into it. You can also use cardboard cutouts instead to create your own, unique designs. Lift the stamp away when you are done. If you want to make a quilted design, let the silicone harden for about 10 to 20 minutes, then dust it with cornstarch.
pair.prefix: You will need to knead it about 20 times or so. You won't pick up all of the cornstarch, which is normal. The dough may look crumbly at first--just keep kneading! You can do this with a rolling pin, a glass, a wine bottle, or even a spray paint can. Keep rolling until you have a sheet a little larger than your phone. It should be about ⅛ inch (0.32 centimeter) thick.
